name: Adenocarcinoma of the Liver and Intrahepatic Biliary Tract

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of adenocarcinoma with biliary differentiation on liver biopsy
Characteristic radiological findings on contrast-enhanced CT or MRI showing mass-forming intrahepatic lesion with biliary ductal involvement
Elevated serum CA 19-9 and/or CEA levels supportive of diagnosis
Exclusion of hepatocellular carcinoma and metastatic adenocarcinoma from other primary sites

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus characteristic imaging findings with exclusion of other primary tumors
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including pathology, radiology, and clinical correlation.

searchTerms: low energy from ongoing health problems

laboratory: Cholestatic liver function test pattern (elevated ALP, GGT, bilirubin)
imaging: Contrast-enhanced CT showing mass-forming intrahepatic lesion with peripheral rim enhancement
MRI with T2 hyperintense lesion and delayed contrast washout
MRCP demonstrating biliary ductal irregularities and obstruction
genetic: Frequent mutations in IDH1/2, FGFR2 fusions in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
KRAS and TP53 mutations in advanced tumors
other: Histopathology showing gland-forming adenocarcinoma with desmoplastic stroma

distinguishingFeatures: Arises from hepatocytes rather than biliary epithelium
Different imaging pattern with arterial phase hyperenhancement
History of primary adenocarcinoma elsewhere (e.g. colon, pancreas)
Multiple liver lesions rather than solitary mass
Immunohistochemistry profile inconsistent with primary biliary origin

redFlags: Progressive cholestasis with worsening liver function
references: Bridgewater J, Galle PR, Khan SA, et al. Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. J Hepatol. 2014;60(6):1268-1289.
